The implementation is complete and all checks pass. Here's a summary of the repaired bridge at `/app/submission/bridge.py`:

## Key repairs vs. the prototype

| Defect in prototype | Fix |
|---|---|
| `dict(fields)` collapsed duplicate fields | Ordered pair list; duplicates preserved and policy-checked per name |
| Stream completion confused with message length | Per-stream terminal tracking (FIN/RESET), `cancelled` / `incomplete` / `rejected` / `forwarded` |
| No frame-shape validation | Unknown frames ignored; shape must be `HEADERS DATA* [HEADERS]`; body ≤ 65536; per-section size ≤ 8192 |
| No field/pseudo-header/target validation | Lowercase-tchar names, octet value rule, pseudo-header order/unicity, method/scheme allow-lists, origin-form path, `*` only for OPTIONS |
| Raw authority used for routing/Host/cache key | Canonical authority (DNS lowercase, IPv4 components, IPv6 `compressed` in brackets, port normalized/default omitted) shared by routing, `Host:` and `cache_key` |
| Route lookups never rejected | Missing route ⇒ `rejected` |
| `content-length`/`te`/prohibited fields forwarded | `content-length` normalized as digit strings and matched to the DATA length; `te` consumed; prohibited names rejected |
| Cookies not merged | Cookie lines joined with `; ` at the first cookie position |
| Trailers unsupported | `x-audit-*` trailers, `trailer:` announcement (dedup, first-occurrence order), single chunk, `0` terminator |
| **Pipelines ordered by stream ID** | **Pipelines now follow FIN order** (offsets/lengths derive from the actual bytes) |

## Validation performed
- Public fixture `check_example.py` passes.
- An independently written re-derivation of the expected ledger agrees on 1500 randomized scenarios (valid and invalid).
- 600-case fuzz run: no crashes, ledger shape always correct.
- Dedicated FIN-order/offset test (200 randomized interleavings), boundary tests (section size 8192/8193, body 65536/65537), and a 20-case acceptance suite covering the whole contract.
- Performance/memory: a 64 MiB input completes in ~0.3 s with ~198 MB RSS; a 256-stream / 8 MiB scenario in ~0.3 s — well inside the 30 s / 20 CPU-s / 512 MiB budgets. No sockets, subprocesses, or filesystem writes.
